The user wants a 600-word technical summary of the provided files. The files are from the "Strata" project — an inference engine for running large MoE (Mixture of Experts) models (specifically Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) on consumer hardware with limited VRAM but ample RAM. Let me analyze the files and produce a detailed technical summary.

The files include:
1. `bench/ctx_bench.py` - A benchmarking harness for measuring streaming chat latency across prompt lengths
2. `bench/expert_gpu_smoke.py` - Dual-GPU regression test
3. `bench/results/` - Various benchmark results (markdown tables with tok/s numbers)
4. `chat.py` - A terminal chat client
5. `docs/DETAILS.md` - Detailed documentation
6. `docs/DUAL-GPU.md` - Dual-GPU research document
7. `include/strata/` - C++ headers for the engine (layers, kernels, caches, graph capture)
8. `include/strata/kernels/` - CUDA kernel headers
9. `include/strata/prefill/` - Prompt processing (chunked, batched)
10. `include/strata/spec/` - Speculative decoding (MTP, suffix lookup)
11. `serve/` - API layer (OpenAI/Anthropic compatible)
12. `ref/` - Reference implementations for validation
13. `README.md` - User-facing documentation

The summary should cover the architectural approach: tiered memory (GPU VRAM for dense weights + expert cache, RAM for all 24,576 experts, SSD for the n-gram table), the techniques used (expert caching with profiles, KV streaming, chunked prefill, speculative decoding with MTP, prompt lookup), and how the benchmark results relate to the design.
